beginner.stem: Which history line belongs to Protactinium?
options: André-Louis Debierne, a colleague of the Curies, found a new radioactive substance in pitchblende residues in 1899 and named it actinium, from the Greek aktis, a ray.
Kasimir Fajans and Oswald Göhring identified a short-lived member of the uranium decay chain in 1913 and called it brevium.
Marguerite Perey, working at the Curie Institute, found a short-lived alkali metal among the decay products of actinium in 1939.
In December 1898, months after polonium, Marie and Pierre Curie announced a second, far more radioactive element in pitchblende.
beginner.explanation: Kasimir Fajans and Oswald Göhring identified a short-lived member of the uranium decay chain in 1913 and called it brevium.

beginner.stem: How does the catalog describe the discovery of Protactinium?
options: Marguerite Perey followed the decay products of actinium-227 at the Curie Institute.
After polonium had been traced into the bismuth fraction of pitchblende, Marie and Pierre Curie found a second excess of activity in the barium fraction.
André-Louis Debierne examined the rare-earth fraction of pitchblende after uranium, polonium, and radium had been removed.
Kasimir Fajans and Oswald Göhring, in 1913, found a short-lived activity in the uranium series, lasting about a minute, and followed it through precipitations.
beginner.explanation: Kasimir Fajans and Oswald Göhring, in 1913, found a short-lived activity in the uranium series, lasting about a minute, and followed it through precipitations.
